decisions.reason: As a visibly launched system in a core office category tied to flexible workplace trends, the firm would be inclined to justify its prior development and marketing investment and treat any weak uptake as temporary.
A chair family sits close to the firm's core competence and broad interior offer, so management would likely continue it to defend earlier commitments and because it remains strategically central.

Floor cushions are a more peripheral accessory line, so despite the initial launch effort the product is easier to abandon because it is less central to the firm's declared direction and less worth escalating.

The sofa received a particularly visible designer-backed launch and fits the firm's main living and lounge business, which makes management likely to persist in order to justify that public commitment.

A high standing table supports the firm's move toward adaptable workplace interiors, so prior investment and strategic fit would push management to keep it and attribute disappointing results to temporary market conditions.
Because the rug collection is more distant from the established offer, management has less strategic reason to keep escalating commitment and is more likely to reallocate resources away from it.
